look_here_first: Grayish thorny shrub with relatively straight stems, scattered less-curved prickles, 1–2 pairs of pinnae, and fragrant pink globose flower heads.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Hays-local + Personal List; Kew accepts species native in Texas; UT PRC documents it as one of NW Hays County's native woody mimosas.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: Installed for active visual learning; broader exact-county reconciliation deferred.

morphology_keys.family_pattern: Fabaceae/Mimosa: bipinnate leaves, pulvini that can drive touch-sensitive movement in several species, globose heads of many tiny flowers, and segmented/prickly legumes. Habit, prickle placement, pinna count, and pod structure are especially useful.
best_field_traits: prickles scattered rather than paired at nodes
pods often longer and stipitate at base
morphology_keys.comparison_training: Best compared with M. texana: borealis is grayer with straighter stems, less-hooked prickles, and usually longer more stipitate pods.
